title: Where two or three (Matthew 18:15–20)
hookLine: go to the one who wronged you, alone; and where two or three gather, he's there
tomorrow: so how many times do you have to forgive the same thing?

cards: Screenshot it. Post it. Tell the whole group chat.
That's one way to handle being wronged, and it's fast.

Matthew eighteen starts somewhere much quieter, and it answers yesterday's question directly: "If thy brother shall trespass against thee, go and tell him his fault between thee and him alone: if he shall hear thee, thou hast gained thy brother."
Start private. And notice the goal. Not winning.

teach.b: Only if that fails does the circle widen: take one or two others along, so that "in the mouth of two or three witnesses every word may be established." Then the church.

teach.h: AS A HEATHEN AND A PUBLICAN?
teach.b: And if he won't hear even the church, let him be to you as a heathen man and a publican. That sounds like a door slamming, but some readers notice how Matthew's Jesus treats publicans, tax collectors: he eats with them.
Then comes the line some people stitch on pillows: "For where two or three are gathered together in my name, there am I in the midst of them."
Here's the thing worth telling a friend: in Matthew, it doesn't come after a worship service.

teach.h: THE ROOM OF THE HARD TALK.
teach.b: It comes right after the steps of a hard conversation.
Two or three is the size of the room where someone says, you hurt me, and someone listens. That small, uncomfortable room is the one he promises to be in.

how: Some Christians pray in pairs or small groups and quote Matthew 18:20 when they gather, and some churches teach its steps, a private talk first, for settling conflicts.

games.q: what does “where two or three” mean?
o: the witnesses a court requires for a verdict
a small gathering where Jesus promises to be
the smallest number for a valid church service

s: Jesus' first step for being wronged is to tell the church
the first step is private: between thee and him alone.
in Matthew, 'where two or three are gathered' comes right after the steps of a hard conversation
it follows the private talk, the witnesses and the church, in Matthew 18:15–20.
Jesus says to cut off anyone who wrongs you
the goal he names is to gain your brother back.

games.q: your roommate keeps eating the food you labeled. you're furious. by Matthew 18's order, what's the first move?
o: a private talk, just the two of you.
a note on the fridge for all the roommates.
bring two friends along, so it's on record.
games.why: first, between thee and him alone. the witnesses come only if that fails, and the goal is to gain her back, not to win.

practice: Two voices sound different from one: they have to wait for each other.

If someone is with you, sit side by side, close enough to hear each other breathe, and say one short line out loud together, slowly, twice; if you pray, it can be today's line, where two or three are gathered together in my name, there am I in the midst of them.
If you're alone, say it once, out loud, and listen to your own voice in the room. Then, in the quiet, let one face come to mind: the person you'd want sitting next to you for it.

wordCard.voice: Where two or three. The small gathering, even the hard conversation, where Jesus promises, there am I in the midst of them.

orig.note: Greek: the word behind church in Matthew 18:17, and in 16:18, on this rock.

carryVoice: Keep this: there am I, even in a room of two, even when it’s awkward. See you tomorrow.
